Kėdainiai: A Lithuanian cultural capital shaped by Scots and the Radziwills
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-16
05:00:00 UTC
14:00:00 KST

This year, the title of Lithuanian Capital of Culture belongs to Kėdainiai, a historic town once ruled by the powerful Radziwill family and shaped by centuries of encounters between different peoples and faiths.
Located in central Lithuania, Kėdainiai is perhaps best known as the country’s “cucumber capital”. But its compact historic centrr offers a richer story, with centuries-old churches and synagogues, distinctive architecture, a forgotten river port and traditional crafts that are still practiced today.
The town’s multicultural heritage is particularly visible in its houses of worship.
According to Rimantas Žirgulis, director of the Kėdainiai Regional Museum, the town was especially diverse during its period of prosperity in the 17th century, when six ethnic and religious communities lived there.
Today, visitors can see an Orthodox church housed in a brick building dating to the second half of the 19th century. The Church of the Transfiguration of Christ retains early 20th-century paintings and valuable icons.
Two Catholic churches also form part of Kėdainiai’s architectural heritage.
The Gothic Church of St George, built in the 15th century, is one of Lithuania’s oldest churches. It contains notable works of art, late Baroque altars and a relic of Blessed Teofilius Matulionis.
The wooden Church of St Joseph, dating to the 18th century, stands with its bell tower near the centre of town. It is known for paintings of St Joseph and the Virgin Mary with the infant Jesus, both featuring ornate metal coverings.
“The Church of St George is a unique 15th-century brick church, one of the oldest in Lithuania. The Church of St Joseph is wooden and dates to the 18th century,” Žirgulis told LRT.lt. “It is also unusual that what looks like a village church stood in the middle of what was, for its time, a large town.”
Kėdainiai’s religious heritage also reflects its once-powerful Protestant communities.
A 17th-century Evangelical Reformed church contains a mausoleum of the Radziwill family and historic pipe organs. The mausoleum was the first restored 17th-century burial site of Lithuanian Grand Duchy nobles in the country. It contains the sarcophagi of several members of the Radziwill family, including Krzysztof I “Perkūnas”, Janusz II, Mikolaj, Jerzy, Stepan and Elzbieta.
The church was once the principal Evangelical Reformed church in Samogitia and later became the main church of the Lithuanian Reformed community, Žirgulis said.
Another landmark is the 17th-century brick Evangelical Lutheran church, which retains original frescoes depicting the apostles Peter and Paul and the four evangelists.
The church reflects the influence of Kėdainiai’s German Lutheran community, Žirgulis said. It stood in Jonušava, then a suburb or separate settlement named after Radziwill nobleman Janusz Radziwill.
The town’s Jewish heritage is equally prominent.
On Senosios Rinkos Square stands a synagogue complex consisting of the Great Summer Synagogue and the Small Winter Synagogue. The Great Synagogue was rebuilt in the Baroque style after a fire in the 18th century and now houses the Kėdainiai Art School. The 19th-century Neoclassical Small Synagogue houses a multicultural centre with an exhibition about the town’s Jewish community and the Holocaust.
The complex is one of only three surviving synagogue complexes in Lithuania.
A historic town centre
The entire Old Town of Kėdainiai is a major attraction. It is a state-protected urban heritage site and one of just seven such sites in Lithuania.
Its compact streets preserve elements of Baroque, Gothic, Renaissance and Neoclassical architecture. Four historic market squares – Senosios Rinkos, Didžiosios Rinkos, Knypavos Rinkos and Janušavos – testify to the town’s role as a regional commercial centre.
Among the landmarks is the former 17th-century town hall on Didžiosios Rinkos Square, one of only three surviving historic town halls in Lithuania.
The Old Town also preserves houses associated with the Kėdainiai Scottish community, including the Grey House.
Another important landmark is Šviesioji Gymnasium, which dates to the middle of the 17th century. The Radziwills planned to develop it into a Protestant institution of higher education, although the ambitious project never came to fruition.
Janusz Radziwill had elevated Kėdainiai’s four-grade school to gymnasium status and hoped eventually to turn it into a Protestant academy capable of competing with the Jesuit academy in Vilnius, Žirgulis said.
When the River Nevėžis was a trade route
Kėdainiai’s history was also shaped by the Nevėžis River.
The site of the former Kėdainiai port, near the present-day Mikalojus Daukša Public Library, recalls the town’s history as a centre of commercial shipping.
Flat-bottomed sailing cargo vessels known as vytinės once carried goods along the river. From Kėdainiai, they travelled to Konigsberg, carrying local and Lithuanian raw materials and returning with a variety of goods and luxury products.
The town’s history of craftsmanship can still be experienced at the Traditional Crafts Centre, housed in the former Arnet House associated with the Scottish community of Kėdainiai.
The centre displays folk art and hosts workshops where visitors can learn traditional crafts that are increasingly rare, Žirgulis said.
The building also has a long religious history. From the second half of the 17th century until the end of the 19th century, it served as the residence of the superintendents of the Evangelical Reformed Church in Samogitia – effectively a regional religious centre.
Kedainiai was also an important centre of Jewish life in Samogitia, with the region’s chief rabbis living in the town.
Traces of that heritage can still be found along Žydų (Jewish) Street, including a surviving house at No. 2 with a wooden annex used for the Jewish festival of Sukkot.
The roof of the structure could be opened, allowing residents to pray beneath the sky without leaving the house, Žirgulis explained. Sukkot commemorates the biblical story of the Israelites’ 40 years of wandering in the desert after leaving Egypt.
A year as cultural capital
Kėdainiai was designated Lithuania’s Capital of Culture for 2026. The yearlong program, titled Kėdainiai Chronicles in Cultural Symbols, highlights the town’s history as a Radziwill city where different ethnic and religious communities lived side by side and where crafts, education and cultural exchange flourished.
The program includes more than 30 projects and 150 events.
August’s program includes the exhibition Universe From a Spiral by Nijolė Šivickas de Mockus, a national painters’ plein air event titled Kėdainiai on Both Sides of the Nevėžis, an exhibition of Impressionist graphics, a traditional weaving project titled Threads That Connect, and a ceramics workshop, Radziwill Symbols in Clay, among other events.

Andrei Vorobyov, governor of the Moscow oblast, wrote on Telegram that an 83-year-old man was killed when a drone hit a private home.
At least five people were killed in attacks on southern Russia’s Rostov region, which borders Ukraine, according to regional authorities.
The drone assault came after Ukrainian authorities said late on Saturday that at least one person was killed and seven were wounded in Russian air attacks.
A woman was killed and six people were wounded in a missile and drone attack on Kryvyi Rih, the hometown of President Volodymyr Zelenskyy in central Ukraine, the region’s governor said.
Officials in the capital said Kyiv was “under ballistic missile attack” late on Saturday, with at least one person wounded and fires sparked at nonresidential sites in the Obolonskyi and Holosiivskyi districts.
Defence and foreign policy analyst Pavel Felgenhauer told Al Jazeera that the targeting of capital cities suggests an escalation in the war. He noted that Ukraine had managed to bypass air defences in the Moscow region, which has the “best and most dense antiair defences in the entirety of Russia”. The attacks did not hit central Moscow but reached the outskirts of the capital, he added.
Separately, Romania’s Ministry of National Defence reported on Sunday that a Spanish F-18 jet on a NATO air policing mission to Romania had shot down a drone breaching its airspace.
Martin O’Donnell, a spokesman for NATO’s military headquarters, said the alliance is prepared to defend itself.
“Additional details regarding Sunday’s incident remain under investigation, but the drone appears to be Russian,” he said.
It was the fourth drone shot down in Romania this year.
The Defence Ministry wrote on social media that the drone came from neighbouring Moldova.
“The surveillance systems of the Ministry of National Defense detected the intrusion of an aerial target into national airspace, coming from the Republic of Moldova,” it said in a statement.
Romanian Defence Minister Radu Miruta congratulated the pilots and military personnel on what he called “a successful mission”.
In July, a Romanian jet shot down a suspected Russian drone, and in May, a stray drone injured two people in the Romanian city of Galati when it collided with a building.
Romania shares a 634km (394-mile) border with Ukraine and has repeatedly seen Russian drones breaching its airspace as Moscow escalates its bombing campaign against Ukrainian civilian and military infrastructure.
Escalating long-range strikes
Russia has maintained near-daily missile and drone strikes across Ukraine since launching its full-scale invasion in early 2022, and areas far from the front lines have frequently come under attack.
The war’s impact has also spread to key regional shipping routes with reports of mines and unmanned sea drones found floating in the Black Sea.
Civilian casualties in Ukraine hit their highest level since 2022 this July, with at least 437 killed and 2,610 injured, according to the United Nations Human Rights Monitoring Mission.
Ukraine has increasingly targeted military, industrial and logistical facilities deep inside Russia, arguing its strikes are a response to Moscow’s ongoing bombardment of Ukrainian towns and infrastructure.

Athens is cleaning its all-marble Olympic stadium for the first time in more than a century
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-16
04:53:01 UTC
13:53:01 KST

Athens is cleaning its all-marble Olympic stadium for the first time in more than a century
ATHENS, Greece (AP) — It has welcomed marathon runners, rock stars and the first modern Olympic athletes. Now it’s time for a monumental scrub.
Athens’ U-shaped Panathenaic Stadium — made entirely of white marble — is getting its first systematic cleaning in more than a century.
Rebuilt for the first modern Olympics in 1896, the site is the ceremonial send-off point for the Olympic flame, including for Los Angeles 2028.
A fresh look in Athens ahead of LA 2028
The stadium is made of the same glittering marble used on the Acropolis, making the cleanup job delicate.
The work is revealing a monument changed by time, weather and millions of visitors. Cleaners in white and blue overalls move across the stadium’s 47 steep tiers with thin spray lances, using clean water at carefully controlled, low pressure. Machines vacuum up the runoff as they go.
“The goal of cleaning is not to make everything white. It’s to remove the dirt and the first layers of organic material that are deposited on the surface,” said Dimitris Selemis, a senior conservator at the site.
“The idea is to clean all the material that (contains) dirt from the surface, so we have a better understanding of the monument,” he said, noting that there is more weed growth and dirt in areas that receive less direct sunlight.
Dealing with chewing gum, high heels and soft-drink stains
Crews are also using steam to remove blotches of chewing gum, which have turned black over time. Stadium officials say chewing gum, high heels and soft-drink stains are among the main culprits that stain the marble.
Now slowly being revealed, the original gleaming look of the venue earned it the widely used Greek nickname “Kallimarmaro,” or beautiful marble.
“We call it Kallimarmaro because it is made of the finest marble, the best that was ever produced ... We are very proud of it,” Isidoros Kouvelos, president of the Hellenic Olympic Committee, told The Associated Press in an interview.
“It needed to be cleaned of everything that has accumulated over all these years,” he said. “This way the Panathenaic Stadium will show all its brilliance and will once again be the foremost monument of humanity for the Olympic Movement.”
Built into a natural ravine, the stadium’s site was used for ancient Greek athletic contests and later Roman spectacles before falling into centuries of disuse.
An African celebration planned in Athens
Since its 1896 revival, it has staged fashion shows, rock concerts, boxing matches and national celebrations — as well as lavish patriotic ceremonies ordered by a military dictatorship in the 1960s.
Today, it’s a popular draw for tourists. Apart from the cleanup, the Kallimarmaro is also getting a new track, upgraded lighting and fresh support facilities. The project is privately funded by a shipping company and overseen by the Hellenic Olympic Committee with guidance from Culture Ministry experts.
The work will continue through 2026 but is currently concentrated on the stadium’s “sling,” or curved end, in time for the next torch-passing ceremony on Sept. 10.
That will be for the Dakar Youth Olympics, scheduled for Oct. 31-Nov. 13 in Senegal, which will be the first Olympic competition ever hosted in Africa.
IOC President Kirsty Coventry, a swimming gold medal winner from Zimbabwe, is due to attend the Sept. 10 ceremony, Kouvelos said.

Last child evacuated from village of Charivne in Kherson region
That is according to the regional police, Ukrinform reports.
"Kherson region police officers evacuated a 47-year-old woman and her 17-year-old son from the frontline village of Charivne. The boy was the last minor remaining in the settlement," the statement said.
The village of Charivne is under constant threat of enemy attacks. Therefore, following a decision by the Kherson Regional Defense Council, the settlement was included in the mandatory evacuation zone. Police officers are helping residents who wish to leave the dangerous area.
Police said that during the evacuation, the 17-year-old was provided with a protective bulletproof vest. They helped the family load their essential belongings and transported the boy and his mother to safety in an armored vehicle. A relative was waiting for them there and drove them to a settlement in the Mykolaiv region.
During the evacuation, the teenager told police officers that he dreams of becoming a history teacher. He plans to apply to one of the higher education institutions in Mykolaiv. The officers wished the future student every success.
Police once again urged families with children not to wait for the security situation to deteriorate and not to delay evacuating from communities in the Kherson region that are under daily attack by Russian forces.
As reported, the villages of Krasnosilske and Charivne in the Borozenske community were added to the list of settlements where mandatory evacuation is being carried out in the Kherson region.

40 Countries, Including Ukraine, Sign Declaration on Intercontinental Missile Tests
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-16
14:43:04 UTC
23:43:04 KST

Taipei welcomed a joint declaration by 40 countries, including Ukraine, on the testing of intercontinental ballistic missiles over the Pacific Ocean.
Taiwan International Radio reported this.
The document, published on August 11, calls on countries to establish transparent and regular mechanisms for advance notification of missile launches to reduce the risk of miscalculations and unintended escalation.
The signatories called for at least 24 hours’ advance notice of tests and other launches of intercontinental ballistic missiles, submarine-launched missiles and space launch vehicles.
The proposal also calls for notifying other countries of the missile class, launch area, flight direction and danger zones for sailors and pilots.
On August 11, China launched a space launch vehicle, but it exploded shortly after liftoff. Taiwan’s Foreign Minister Lin Chia-lung condemned Beijing’s actions.
The following day, August 12, North Korea launched a ballistic missile from its east coast toward the Sea of Japan.
Hwasong-11D missile launch, May 2024. Photo: KCNA
This was North Korea’s ninth ballistic missile launch since the beginning of 2026.
According to preliminary Japanese estimates, the missile traveled about 690 km and reached a maximum altitude of approximately 90 km. It fell into the Sea of Japan outside Japan’s exclusive economic zone.
Lin Chia-lung said Beijing is attempting to unilaterally change the status quo in the Taiwan Strait and the Indo-Pacific region through military pressure, economic coercion and “gray-zone” tactics.

Slovakia’s STV Machinery Produces Two Prototypes of New BMP-1 Hull
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-16
14:02:34 UTC
23:02:34 KST

Slovak company STV Machinery is preparing for serial production of new armored hulls for BMP-1 infantry fighting vehicles.
The Future Army publication reported this.
The first several dozen hulls are planned for production in 2026-2027.
STV Machinery has already produced two prototypes. The first was intended for testing final assembly and weapons installation, while the second is being used for physical and load testing.
The company operates at the site of the former ZŤS defense plant in Dubnica nad Váhom. During the Czechoslovak era, Soviet BMP-1 and BMP-2 vehicles were produced there.
Development of the new hull began in 2024 at the request of Czech company STV Group. As part of the project, the companies fully digitized the design, prepared new production documentation and developed welding equipment.
The new hull was created based on the BMP-1 design, which remains widespread around the world, but was adapted to modern requirements. In particular, the manufacturer plans to use modern armor materials used in Western armored combat vehicles.
“We are currently actively preparing for serial production of the first several dozen units,” said Pavel Beran, director of special projects at STV Group.
The company is also developing vehicles for different powerplant configurations. Customers will be able to choose between different engines, including powerplants manufactured in the West.
At the same time, STV Group does not disclose information about potential customers for the new vehicles. According to Beran, the company does not disclose details about specific customers or contract terms for security reasons and due to commercial confidentiality.
Earlier, Militarnyi reported that Slovak company STV Machinery had already received its first order from a foreign customer for serial production of BMP-1 hulls.

U.S. Army to Outsource Helicopter Pilot Training to Private Company
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-16
13:21:23 UTC
22:21:23 KST

The U.S. Army will outsource the initial training of military pilots to private contractor M1 Support Services.
The U.S. Department of War announced the contract.
Under the Flight School Next program, the company will train future Army helicopter pilots and provide aircraft, maintenance, simulators, flight training and academic instruction.
Training will take place at Fort Rucker, Alabama.
Each year, the private contractor will train 800-1,500 pilots. The U.S. Army will retain control over training standards, safety requirements and training outcomes.
For the initial flight-training phase, M1 will use Robinson R66 light single-engine helicopters, which will replace the UH-72 Lakota.
Earlier, Militarnyi reported that the U.S. Air Force had awarded a contract to a private company to train F-35 fighter pilots.
The use of private contractors in military pilot training in the United States has a long history.
Traditionally, private companies helped provide military aviation training by maintaining aircraft, operating simulators and handling logistics, but did not directly conduct flight training for cadets. One notable example is DynCorp International, founded in 1946, which provided aviation services to the U.S. government for decades.
In addition to M1 Support Services, the United States has developed an entire ecosystem of private companies that have participated in military pilot training for decades, primarily for the Air Force, Navy and Army. The Canadian company CAE has become the largest and one of the most influential companies in this market.
In 2021, CAE made a major acquisition of L3Harris Technologies’ military training division for $1.05 billion. The deal covered three key assets: Doss Aviation, a provider of initial flight training for the U.S. Air Force; AMI, a manufacturer of simulation equipment; and Link Simulation & Training, one of the leading providers of military training solutions in the United States.
After the deal was completed, CAE became a prime contractor or key subcontractor in a number of programs, including SCARS, the U.S. Air Force’s single simulator architecture; the F-16 simulator training program; F/A-18 aircrew training systems for the Navy and Marine Corps; the Air Force’s initial flight training program; training for operators of the ground-based strategic deterrent GBSD system; and a training system for B-2 bombers.

Ukraine Sends Record 600 Drones Toward Moscow Region
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-16
12:41:30 UTC
21:41:30 KST

According to the mayor of Moscow, 600 Ukrainian drones were detected over a 24-hour period “in the direction of the Moscow region.” This is the largest number of Ukrainian strike drones to have headed toward the Russian capital since the beginning of the war.
Moscow Mayor Sergei Sobyanin reported the drone attack on his Telegram channel.
During the attack, Ukraine’s Defense Forces struck Wildberries warehouses in Koledino and the Severnoye Domodedovo logistics facility near Moscow.
This suggests that the intensity of Ukraine’s long-range strikes continues to increase in August. During July, 6,225 drones were launched toward Moscow and the Moscow region, while in just the first 16 days of August, at least 4,327 UAVs were launched toward the Moscow region.
The average daily number of drones targeting Moscow and neighboring regions increased from approximately 201 in July to 290 in the first half of August, an increase of nearly 44%.
The figures are part of a broader trend of intensifying Ukrainian strikes. OSINT analysts from the Oko Gora channel recorded 65 confirmed strikes by Ukrainian long-range drones and missiles in July, 55% more than in June.
The targets included 17 oil refineries, 16 logistics centers, 10 oil depots, nine ports, four defense industry enterprises, three vessels and two airfields.
These figures do not include the campaign of strikes against vessels in the Sea of Azov and Black Sea or attacks on temporarily occupied territories.
For comparison, during the first 15 days of August, analysts from ExileNova+ had already recorded at least 43 facilities struck by long-range drones and missiles.
These included 22 logistics infrastructure facilities, as well as oil refineries and military airfields. Compared with July, the average daily rate of confirmed strikes increased by approximately 37%.
Ukraine first surpassed Russia in the number of long-range drones launched in March 2026 and has maintained this lead consistently since May. At the same time, Russian forces have begun shifting their focus to the use of large numbers of jet-powered drones, which are more difficult to counter with interceptor drones.
On August 15, Flamingo cruise missiles struck an industrial site in Samara that houses the Aviakor and Progress Rocket Space Centre enterprises. The latter produces Soyuz-2 launch vehicles.
According to the Varta OSINT project, Progress is one of the key enterprises in Russia’s rocket and space industry. The company develops and produces launch vehicles, including the Soyuz-2 family, which are used to launch Russia’s equivalent of Starlink, the Rassvet communications satellites.

Ukrainian Navy Strikes Bastion Missile System Positions in Crimea
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-16
12:02:33 UTC
21:02:33 KST

In the early hours of August 16, Ukrainian Navy units struck the launch positions and deployment site of a Bastion coastal missile system in temporarily occupied Crimea.
The video of the strike was released by the Ukrainian Navy press service.
Judging by the released video, FP-2 drones were used in the strike. According to the General Staff, the strike took place near the village of Rezervne, not far from Sevastopol.
The Navy said the strike caused significant losses in equipment and personnel. The final extent of the enemy’s losses is still being determined.
The Bastion system was originally intended to engage surface ships, but Russia uses it to strike ground targets in Ukraine with P-800 Oniks and 3M22 Zircon missiles.
The system is produced in two variants: the mobile Bastion-P and the stationary, or silo-based, Bastion-S, with the latter primarily intended for export. Each Bastion-P launcher carries two missiles in transport-launch containers for vertical launch.
The Oniks anti-ship missile is 8.9 meters long and has a diameter of 0.7 meters. Its launch weight is 3 tons, and its wingspan is 1.7 meters. The high-explosive penetrating warhead weighs 300 kg. The engine allows the missile to reach a maximum speed of up to Mach 2.6, or 3,182 km/h, at high altitude, and about Mach 2, or 2,448 km/h, near the surface.
Thanks to their supersonic speed and ability to fly at extremely low altitudes, missiles of this type are difficult targets to intercept. Russian forces typically use them to strike Odesa and coastal areas.
The 3M22 Zircon anti-ship missile was developed for use with the 3S14 universal vertical launch system installed on ships, but was later adapted for launch from ground-based systems.
The missile’s exact specifications are unknown. By studying fragments of downed missiles, Ukrainian researchers have established that the warhead weighs approximately 150-200 kg, of which about 40-80 kg is explosive.
According to the latest research, the Zircon is likely not a hypersonic cruise missile but rather a ballistic missile that uses a quasi-ballistic trajectory.
For more details about the system, see our special report, “Russia’s Bastion: Threat to Ukraine and the Capabilities of the Missile System.“

The Times: Ukraine Used British Nyan Drones to Attack Oil Refineries
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-16
11:22:26 UTC
20:22:26 KST

Ukraine used British-made Nyan attack drones to strike Russian oil refineries in Volgograd and Yaroslavl.
The Times reported the attacks.
The Nyan drone was developed by British company Callen-Lenz, which is part of FalconWorks, the technology division of BAE Systems.
The drone has a wingspan of 2.9 meters and a maximum takeoff weight of more than 75 kg. It is launched using a pneumatic catapult.
The aircraft is powered by a single gas turbine engine. It has a cruising speed of 120 knots, or about 222 km/h, and a reported range of more than 250 km.
The drone can carry up to 20 kg of payload. Its modular design allows different equipment to be installed depending on the mission.
Nyan drones have been in service with the Ukrainian Defense Forces for some time.
In late June 2024, an identical drone was found on Russian territory. At the time, it was mistakenly identified as a new Ukrainian kamikaze drone.
It later emerged that the drone is manufactured by British company Callen-Lenz at a facility in Wiltshire. In addition to Ukraine, Nyan drones have also entered service with the British Army.
The first unit to receive these drones was the 26th Regiment Royal Artillery, part of the 3rd Division. The British military uses Nyan as a long-range strike system and to complement the artillery capabilities of its units.
The drone was initially tested in Estonia during the annual Spring Storm exercises, where the Royal Artillery conducted test launches and practiced coordination. Following the trials, the regiment officially adopted the Nyan UAV into service.
Its use is expected to expand to other units in the future.
To expand the drone’s operational capabilities, the British Army, together with the Royal Navy, also tested launching it from a surface vessel.
In June 2026, a catapult was installed on the experimental vessel XV Patrick Blackett, from which a Nyan drone was launched.
Back in February 2026, Callen-Lenz was awarded a £4.99 million contract (approximately $6.7 million) by the UK Ministry of Defence to supply Nyan OWE systems to enhance deep-strike capabilities.
According to the official explanation, Nyan became the only mass-produced system of its class registered in the Military Aircraft Register. This was a key factor in selecting the system for rapid deployment.

U.S. Navy May Redesign Ford-Class Aircraft Carriers to Suit Trump’s Preferences
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-16
10:33:29 UTC
19:33:29 KST

The U.S. Navy is considering major changes to the design of its new Ford-class nuclear-powered aircraft carriers to better match President Donald Trump’s aesthetic preferences.
The Washington Post reported this, citing seven current and former U.S. officials familiar with the matter.
According to the officials, Trump wants the new carriers to look more like the warships that were in service during World War II.
The U.S. Navy is assessing whether it would make sense to move the carrier’s multi-level island, which serves as the ship’s command center, forward toward the middle of the ship. On the new Ford-class carriers, the island is located closer to the stern.
On carriers of this class, the island was moved aft to improve operational efficiency and safety. This configuration not only freed up additional deck space for aircraft operations around the catapults and reduced the time required to position aircraft for launch, but also improved landing safety by reducing turbulence in the landing area as aircraft approached the carrier.
The issue was already studied during Trump’s first term. A study conducted at the time concluded that relocating the island could cost billions of dollars and result in significant delays to the carrier program.
In addition, on August 13, Trump issued a national security memorandum directing the Navy to develop a plan to replace the highly efficient electromagnetic aircraft launch system with conventional steam catapults on future aircraft carriers. The document states that the administration favors “proven, reliable, and affordable technologies and ship designs.” Such a change could also cost billions of dollars and further exacerbate the chronic delays affecting the U.S. shipbuilding industry.
Construction of the lead Ford-class aircraft carrier, USS Gerald R. Ford, took 17 years. Three more ships of the class are currently at various stages of construction. USS John F. Kennedy is undergoing sea trials and nearing commissioning, while USS Enterprise and USS Doris Miller are under construction.
According to estimates by the U.S. Congressional Budget Office and the Navy’s latest shipbuilding plan, each future Ford-class aircraft carrier could cost approximately $22 billion.
As the publication notes, Trump has repeatedly expressed an interest in the design of U.S. Navy warships. Last year, he unveiled plans for a new class of Trump-class battleships that would lead his proposed “Golden Fleet.”
If the planned design is built, the nuclear-powered battleship, with a full-load displacement of 35,000 tons, would become the most heavily armed surface combatant ever built for the U.S. Navy.
It is planned to be equipped with surface-to-air and anti-ship missiles, land-attack missiles, hypersonic weapons, nuclear-armed cruise missiles, high-powered laser systems, and a railgun – an electromagnetic weapon.
The Congressional Budget Office estimates that building the 15 planned Trump-class battleships between 2028 and 2056 would cost approximately $275 billion. After completion of the lead ship, estimated at $23.4 billion, each subsequent ship is projected to cost about $18 billion.

Drone Attack Sparks Fire at Kamensky Combine Chemical Plant in Rostov Oblast
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-16
10:06:39 UTC
19:06:39 KST

The Ukrainian Defense Forces reportedly struck the Kamensky Combine chemical plant in Rostov Oblast, Russia.
The strike is supported by an unusually strong heat signature detected at the facility by NASA’s FIRMS satellite monitoring system.
The heat signature appeared around the same time Rostov Oblast Governor Yuri Slyusar reported a Ukrainian drone attack on the region during the night of August 16.
More than 150 drones were reportedly destroyed over the region.
NASA’s FIRMS detected the thermal signature at 1:14 a.m. on August 16. It remained visible and expanded until 2:20 a.m.
According to the OSINT source VARTA, the Kamensky Combine is one of the largest chemical enterprises in southern Russia and is designated as a city-forming enterprise.
The plant is located at coordinates 48.29943029832428, 40.17984650497104, approximately 10–15 km from the Ukrainian state border.
Due to its proximity to Ukraine, the facility is within range of a significant number of weapons systems used by the Ukrainian Defense Forces.
The plant’s main activity is the production of military goods. The facility manufactures artillery shells, gunpowder, explosives, detonators, fuses, primers, precursors, and other ammunition components.
In addition to military products, the facility manufactures a wide range of chemical products, including plastics and synthetic resins, alcohols, phenols, and their derivatives.
The plant has previously been targeted by Ukrainian aircraft. On December 20, 2024, the Ukrainian Air Force attacked the facility with Storm Shadow cruise missiles.
At the time, analysts from the CyberBoroshno group published a satellite image showing critical damage to two buildings at the plant’s production site.

Poland Begins Developing Long-Range Strike Capabilities Beyond 1,000 km
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-16
09:22:50 UTC
18:22:50 KST

Poland aims to develop the capability to conduct precision strikes against targets more than 1,000 kilometers away. The country is considering strike drones, cruise missiles, and ballistic missiles as potential weapons.
Brigadier General Grzegorz Potrzuski, Head of the Planning and Programming Directorate for the Development of the Polish Armed Forces, said this in an interview with Defence24.
According to Potrzuski, Poland’s land forces can currently strike ground targets at ranges of around 300 kilometers using U.S.-made ATACMS and South Korean CTM-290 missiles. However, the experience of the Russia-Ukraine war has shown the need for precision-strike weapons capable of reaching much greater distances.
In addition to ground-based systems, the Polish Armed Forces will also receive long-range air-launched cruise missiles. In May 2024, Poland’s Ministry of National Defence signed a contract for the delivery of several hundred U.S.-made AGM-158 JASSM-ER air-to-surface cruise missiles.
The contract is reportedly worth approximately $735 million. Deliveries are scheduled to take place from 2026 to 2030.
The AGM-158 JASSM-ER has a range of up to 1,000 kilometers and carries a 450 kg warhead. The missile uses GPS guidance, while during the terminal phase of flight, it employs an infrared seeker to locate and acquire the target.
According to the brigadier general, the General Staff of the Polish Armed Forces is already working on a doctrine for conducting deep precision strikes. The doctrine is intended to establish the principles for developing the required capabilities and to define requirements for the Polish defense industry regarding future weapon systems for the Polish Armed Forces.
To carry out these missions, Poland does not plan to create additional military units. Instead, specialized units will be established within existing structures, with their capabilities gradually expanded until they reach full operational readiness.
One of the first steps in developing Poland’s domestic missile industry is expected to be the establishment of a joint venture to produce CGR-080 rockets, with a range of approximately 80 kilometers, for the Homar-K multiple launch rocket system (MLRS).
Over the next several years, Polish companies are expected to master their production and establish a technological foundation for the further development of the country’s missile capabilities.
Meanwhile, Poland is assessing the availability and development potential of strike UAVs, cruise missiles, and ballistic missiles. The country may pursue these projects independently or in cooperation with foreign allies.
According to the general, in addition to developing strike capabilities, Poland also needs to strengthen its intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance capabilities required to detect targets, determine their coordinates, and assess the results of strikes.

Spanish Hornet Shoots Down Drone Over Romania After It Entered From Moldova
Unknown

08:11:55 UTC
17:11:55 KST

On the night of August 16, a Spanish EF-18 fighter jet shot down a drone that had entered Romanian airspace from Moldova.
Romania’s Ministry of National Defence confirmed the incident.
The ministry’s surveillance systems detected the drone at 4:44 a.m., about 24 km (15 miles) north of the city of Galați.
A Spanish EF-18 fighter jet, deployed at Mihail Kogălniceanu Air Base as part of NATO’s air policing mission, established radar contact with the target and received authorization to engage it.
At 5:01 a.m., the fighter jet shot down the drone. Romania’s Ministry of National Defence said the aircraft destroyed the drone over an uninhabited area.
The possible crash site was identified between the villages of Băleni and Cudalbi in Galați County. The area is away from populated areas. Preliminary reports indicate that there were no casualties and no damage to infrastructure.
This is the fourth drone Romania has shot down in its airspace in 2026. On July 24, 25, and 26, Romanian F-16 fighter jets shot down three Russian drones after they entered Romanian airspace.
In addition, on May 19, 2026, a Romanian F-16 from the “Carpathian Vipers” unit shot down a drone in Estonian airspace. The drone had previously flown about 80 km into Estonian territory.
The handover ceremony took place on July 31, 2026, at Borcea Air Base, also known as Fetești Air Base.
Spain has deployed seven EF-18M Hornet fighter jets to Romania. The deployment also includes three NH-90 helicopters tasked with counter-drone operations and one A400M tanker aircraft for aerial refueling.
This is the fourth deployment of Spanish forces to Romania. Previous deployments took place in 2021, 2024, and February 2026.
The deployment is part of Spain’s national “Persistent Effort” operation and is expected to continue until December 2026.
The mission is formally classified not as traditional Air Policing, but as part of NATO’s broader Air Defence concept within the Integrated Air and Missile Defence (IAMD) system.

More Than 1,600 Civilians Affected by Russian Mines
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-16
07:57:28 UTC
16:57:28 KST

Since the beginning of Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine, 1,645 civilians have been affected by landmines and explosive remnants of war. Among them are 170 children and 1,475 adults.
The Ministry of Defence of Ukraine reported this.
Information about such incidents is processed by the Main Directorate for Mine Action, Civil Protection and Environmental Safety. After verification, the data is entered into the information management system for mine action. This, in particular, enables victims to receive financial assistance from international organizations.
Between 2023 and 2026, 185 people affected by mine-related incidents received assistance from international organizations totaling more than UAH 3.4 million.
The assistance covers medical treatment and rehabilitation expenses, as well as the purchase of equipment for remote learning and work for people with mine and explosive injuries.
The experience of large-scale armed conflicts shows that the threat posed by landmines can persist for decades after hostilities have ended.
Croatia needed more than 30 years to clear all known mine-contaminated areas affected by the 1991–1995 War of Independence.
In 1996, the UN Mine Action Centre preliminarily estimated that 13,000 km² of the country’s territory was potentially contaminated. Following systematic surveys, this figure was revised to 1,174 km² as of 2005.
Over the course of the demining operations in Croatia, nearly 107,000 mines and more than 470,000 unexploded ordnance items were discovered and cleared.
By comparison, as of April 2025, approximately 139,000 km² of Ukraine’s territory was considered potentially contaminated with explosive remnants of war.
Throughout 2025, demining units of Ukraine’s Ministry of Defence cleared 662.7 km² of liberated territory. Another approximately 4,541 km² of Ukrainian land was returned to use after being surveyed.
Overall, since the beginning of the full-scale invasion, Ukraine has returned more than 40,000 km² of territory to use.

Gallery: Pärnu Literature Festival faces an uncertain future
The Pärnu Literature Festival took place for the sixth time on Saturday in Estonia's summer capital, but organizers say it could be the last due to a lack of funding.
The festival opened with the placing of a flower wreath on the head of the statue of writer and poet Lydia Koidula (1843-1886) in Koidula Park, where the event takes place.
The 12-hour festival included lectures, meetings with authors, a book fair and a special children's and youth area.
However, festival organiser Merle Jantson said holding the event has become increasingly difficult financially with each passing year. This year's festival may be the last.
"This is a programme that runs from noon until midnight, the aim of which is to value and introduce the Estonian language, Estonian literature and Estonian writers," she said.

Under the influence of the low-pressure system, weather along the southern China coast would become unsettled with increasing showers and squally thunderstorms midweek, the Observatory said.

Australia gun buyback spurred by Bondi attack to start in November, PM says
Australia introduced measures to reduce gun ownership following a deadly attack on Sydney’s Bondi Beach last year.
Australia’s prime minister has said that New South Wales will begin a gun buyback scheme in November as part of a nationwide response to last year’s deadly Sydney beach attack.
The gun buyback scheme will be accompanied by tighter checks for gun licences and a crackdown on hate, Prime Minister Anthony Albanese said on Sunday.

The measures targeting firearm ownership are a reaction to the December 14, 2025, gun attack at a Bondi Beach Hanukkah celebration in Sydney, New South Wales, that killed 15 people.
The alleged gunmen used powerful firearms that were legally obtained.
Australians owned a record 4.1 million firearms last year, the government has said, with more than 1.1 million of those in New South Wales, the country’s most populous state.
New South Wales’ gun buyback scheme is scheduled to start on November 2, and will see the state offer owners up to 1,000 Australian dollars ($700) per handgun or rifle handed in.
“Australians are quite rightly proud of our gun laws, but the fact is there are more guns in Australia today than there were at the time of dealing with the Port Arthur gun buyback,” Albanese said in televised remarks.
In the 1996 Port Arthur attack, a lone gunman killed 35 people and led to sweeping restrictions on ownership of automatic and semi-automatic firearms in Australia.
Since the Bondi Beach attack, New South Wales state has introduced its own laws limiting gun ownership to four guns per person.
Police say the attack was carried out by a father and son duo and was inspired by ISIL (ISIS). The surviving suspect, Naveed Akram, 24, is yet to enter pleas to several charges, including 15 counts of murder.

Miami to decide fate of stunning stadium where speedboats raced and Jimmy Buffett played
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-16
04:23:01 UTC
13:23:01 KST

Miami to decide fate of stunning stadium where speedboats raced and Jimmy Buffett played
MIAMI (AP) — The Miami Marine Stadium, considered a masterpiece of midcentury Brutalist architecture with its massive cantilevered roof and a stunning view of the city, opened in 1963 as the nation’s only race venue for powerboats, a major symbol of South Florida.
The historic gem designed by a Cuban refugee was the backdrop of Elvis Presley’s 1967 film “Clambake” and a beloved venue of Gloria Estefan and the late Jimmy Buffett, who performed on a movable, floating stage.
But since closing in 1992 after suffering serious damage during Hurricane Andrew, the 6,500-seat venue has fallen into disarray and today is fenced off and covered in graffiti despite being listed on the U.S. National Register of Historic Places.
On Tuesday, voters will decide whether to allow the city to partner with a private company to return the unique stadium situated on Virginia Key across the water from downtown Miami to its former glory.
President Richard Nixon and Sammy Davis Jr. appeared together at the stadium during a 1972 campaign rally to support Nixon’s reelection bid. And residents would gather for Easter sunrise services, as well as celebrate Our Lady of Charity, a representation of the Virgin Mary honored by many Cubans and Cuban Americans.
“It encapsulated a time period in Miami that’s incredibly unique with an incredible story that touches all Miamians,” Miami Commissioner Damian Pardo said. “So this is really a place that connects with Miami at a very deep and personal level.”
The stadium has a rich history in Miami
Hilario Candela was in his late 20s and a recent refugee from the Cuban Revolution when he designed the structure. He spent decades designing buildings around Miami and led community efforts to restore the marine stadium until his death in 2022.
When it was added to the National Park Service’s National Register of Historic Places in 2018, then-Secretary of State Ken Detzner called the stadium “one of the state of Florida’s most unique architectural and historic resources,” and “an ambitious example of mid-century Modernist architecture” that represented the “multi-cultural influences evolving in the city of Miami during the 1960s.”
The year before his 2023 passing, Buffett wrote a letter to Miami officials, urging them to save the “little cathedral of musical fun.” The Mayor of Margaritaville described a 1985 concert at the marine stadium that ended with him jumping off the floating stage into the surrounding water, joining cheering swimmers and boaters.
“Those were the ‘Miami Vice’ days, and Don Johnson introduced us,” Buffett wrote of the actor in the popular 1980s television crime drama. “WITCO Desperadoes from Trinidad opened the show, and the Coral Reefer Band finished the night with what I think was one of the most fun shows, for band and fans, that I have ever done.”
Buffett’s daughter, Savannah, continues to work with Restore Miami Marine Stadium. The group’s co-founder, Donald Worth, began a mission to save the stadium in 2008, shortly after city officials at the time announced plans to tear it down.
“The architecture gives it the wow, the history gives it its soul,” Worth said. “It’s just a special, magical place, and so many people in Miami have had such memorable experiences there.”
Voters will help decide the stadium’s future
Breakwater Hospitality Group co-founder Emi Guerra, who’s working with the company selected to partner with the city, said the stadium’s view of the city skyline and its location right off Biscayne Bay could make it an entertainment destination that rivals Denver’s Red Rocks Amphitheatre, an open-air venue built into the side of a mountain.
“There’s just something here that can’t be duplicated, and that’s the view,” Guerra said of the marine stadium.
Guerra said he can understand the cynicism felt by some voters, but he points out that this isn’t a developer land grab to build more condos. The city of Miami will retain complete ownership of the stadium and surrounding area, and the management company will be stewards of the city’s vision, Guerra said.
“When it’s something that’s historic, you have two options: restore it or let it rot,” Guerra said.
Ernesto Cuesta, head of the Brickell Homeowners Association, sees another option.
He said the group supports the preservation of a historical landmark, but members are worried about how noise and traffic from a large-scale event space will affect residents across the bay and nearby wildlife. He said he’d prefer a park with more green spaces.
Restoration plans aim to honor the stadium’s past
Despite sitting unused for more than three decades, multiple studies have shown that the stadium remains structurally safe.
Project architect Richard Heisenbottle, who has previously worked to restore other Miami landmarks, said he hopes reviving the marine stadium will honor its original architect.
He said renovations will have to include modern amenities and accessibility requirements, but the galvanized steel rebar used to reinforce the concrete during its original construction has protected the stadium from serious deterioration. Completed construction documents for the restorations have already been permitted by the city of Miami, he said.
Miami Commissioner Pardo said a significant hurdle to reopening the stadium previously has been the city government simply not having the capacity to properly run a major event space.
The referendum going before Miami voters on Tuesday would allow the city to enter into a management agreement.
The private company would develop the stadium’s large parking area into a flex park that includes public recreational facilities and a special events space. The city would collect revenue from events to fund the stadium repairs and upgrades, while paying the company a management fee. The total cost of the project hasn’t been determined, but Pardo insisted it will not be borne by taxpayers at all.
“It’s the right time to finally do this,” Pardo said.

Brown stands out for Cowboys with 2 TD catches in 17-7 win over Seahawks
SEATTLE (AP) — Rookie Camden Brown had two touchdown catches, including a diving, one-handed snag, to help lead the Dallas Cowboys past the Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks 17-7 on Saturday night in the preseason opener for both team.
Brown caught a 39-yard pass from Sam Howell in the second quarter to put Dallas up 10-7. On the first drive of the third quarter, Brown snared a 2-yard fade from Joe Milton in the back left corner of the end zone.
“Really good day,” said Cowboys coach Brian Schottenheimer. “He’s got to keep stacking them, but he’s been doing it.”
An undrafted free agent who started his career at Auburn before transferring to Georgia Southern, Brown has stood out throughout training camp. The 6-foot-2, 204-pound wide receiver has made good use of his frame, and demonstrated on Saturday he can also do so in an NFL game.
“The game’s not too big for him,” Schottenheimer said. “He does it every day in practice, we see it all the time.”
Milton, who’s entering his third pro season and second with Dallas, was impressive in his bid to be the Cowboys’ backup quarterback behind Dak Prescott. The 2024 sixth-round draft pick completed six of his first eight passes against the Seahawks’ backup cornerbacks, and finished 12 of 15 for 107 yards and the TD to Brown.
Howell, who is competing with Milton for the Cowboys’ No. 2 job, was 8 of 12 for 94 yards and his touchdown pass to Brown.
“They just hung in there and made the throws when they had to make them,” Schottenheimer said about his quarterbacks, “and they were both very efficient.”
With Sam Darnold sitting out, Seattle rotated its backup quarterbacks throughout the night. Drew Lock led the Seahawks on a 13-play, 80-yard scoring drive to open the game. It was capped by a 5-yard touchdown catch by Montorie Foster Jr.
“It was a tight window, too,” Foster said. “Shoutout to Drew. On that plant, I knew the ball was going to be right there. So, I was just ready for it.”
Brandon Aubrey converted a 29-yard field goal to cut Seattle’s lead to 7-3 early in the second quarter. The Seahawks responded with a 15-play drive, but Jason Myers pushed a 45-yard attempt wide right before Brown caught his first touchdown pass.
Jalen Milroe, currently entrenched as Seattle’s third-string quarterback, was 5 of 8 for 36 yards. Lock was 9 of 13 for 40 yards and a touchdown.
Cowboys running back Jaydon Blue, who is competing with Phil Mafah to be Javonte Williams’ backup, was stifled by Seattle’s defense. Blue had 19 yards on eight carries.
George Holani, one of the few healthy Seahawks running backs, paced Seattle with 12 carries for 42 yards. Zach Charbonnet, Emanuel Wilson and 2026 first-round pick Jadarian Price – all of whom could be options for Seattle this season at running back – sat out with injuries.
Tyrice Knight led the Seahawks with 10 tackles, all in the first half. Knight, who has 145 tackles over the last two seasons, is pleased with his progress since the Seahawks selected in the fourth round in 2024.
“Probably the biggest step for me is just being more decisive,” Knight said. “Just like how I was more (decisive) at UTEP, bringing that same game to the NFL and then just playing downhill more and being ahead of the play.”
Curtis Robinson paced the Cowboys with eight tackles.
Foster had a team-high five catches for 36 yards for Seattle. Malik Davis ran for 39 yards on seven carries for Dallas.
Seattle’s Rashad Rochelle had a 52-yard punt return in the third quarter.
The teams combined for 21 penalties and 174 penalty yards
Backing Arnold
Milroe, who was a college teammate of Terrion Arnold for three seasons at Alabama, supported Seattle’s decision to enter an agreement with the cornerback. Arnold is facing eight felony charges stemming from allegations he orchestrated the abduction and beating of three men in February.
“That’s my dog. I’m very happy that he’s going to be a Seahawk,” Milroe said. “I think now, it’s just showing him the way of how we do things. And, that’s the move-forward process.”
Injuries
Seahawks: Tackle Amari Kight (leg) left in the second quarter and put ice on his lower leg on the sideline. Edge rusher Jared Ivey went into the injury tent in the third quarter, but returned.
Cowboys: Mafah (chest) exited in the third quarter and was ruled out. Schottenheimer said he talked with Mafah postgame, and that he is OK.
Up next
Cowboys: At Arizona on Aug. 22.
Seahawks: At Tennessee on Aug. 23.

Mackenzie Dern wins 115-pound title defense at UFC 330; Makhachev goes for record win streak
Unknown

Make it 17 straight! Makhachev sets UFC record for consecutive wins in welterweight title defense
PHILADELPHIA (AP) — The bridge of Islam Makhachev’s nose, right cheek and forehead were scraped or sliced open and his left cheek sported a baseball-sized bruise after taking a few too many brutal blows to the face.
He may not have looked the part, yet Makhachev was again a winner — all while toppling one of UFC’s most enduring records.
Makhachev set the UFC record with his 17th straight victory, reaching the milestone with a unanimous decision over Ian Machado Garry to successfully defend his 170-pound championship in the main event of UFC 330 on Saturday night.
Makhachev won 49-46 on two scorecards and 48-47 on the third in a competitive five-round fight that never rose to the level of greatness.
“He gave me a hard time,” Makhachev said, “but I still prove it every fight.”
Makhachev (29-1) was tied with UFC Hall of Famer Anderson Silva with 16 straight victories and has not lost since UFC 192 in 2015. Makhachev won the welterweight crown in his first attempt when he beat Jack Della Maddalena at UFC 322 in November 2025.
He took his share of head kicks in his first title defense, notably in the third round that did most of the cosmetic damage, yet bested a record set by Silva that had stood for 13 years.
“If he keeps going like he says he’s going to keep going, it might never be beaten,” UFC CEO Dana White said.
The 34-year-old Makhachev nearly ended the fight in the second when he threw his left foot and caught Machado Garry flush with a headkick that dropped the challenger to his rear end. Makhachev pounced with a series of punches that had the sellout crowd of 19,238 fans roaring in anticipation of a quick finish, only for Machado Garry — serenaded throughout with obscenity-laced chants — to hold on and finish the round.
Machado Garry (17-2) won the third round on all three scorecards and rallied in the fifth round with seven significant strikes landed to none for Makhachev.
Yet it wasn’t enough to topple one of UFC’s great fighters.
“I believed in my heart and soul I was better than him tonight, and he won,” Machado Garry said. “No complaints, no excuses. I’m 28, I have a decade of domination already. This man won tonight.”
Makhachev — who held the lightweight championship and has seven total wins in title fights — continues to dominate no matter the weight class.
Dern defends 115-pound title on first try
Mackenzie Dern successfully defended the 115-pound championship in her first title defense with a unanimous decision victory over Gillian Robertson that could set her up for a fight with division great Zhang Weili.
Dern (17-5) won the vacant strawweight belt in her last fight at UFC 321 and won a lopsided and lackluster first defense against Robertson.
Dern won 49-46 on two scorecards and 48-47 on the third in the five-round fight.
“I wanted to get the submission with Gillian,” Dern said. “I definitely wanted to submit her. That was the goal.”
Dern nearly made Robertson (17-9) tap in the first round with a choke hold that about turned the challenger’s face as pinkish-red as her braided hair. Dern might have won the bout had it stretched even another 30 seconds, but Robertson was saved by the bell.
Too bad the fight didn’t end there.
The next four rounds were relatively uneventful, and the title match slowed to a near complete stop as they mostly locked up on the canvas with barely a strike thrown.
Dern’s 7-year-old daughter peered her head over the barricade from her front row seat and shouted encouragement each time mom got close to her side of the cage. The little girl could be heard well over a rowdy crowd that had about been lulled into passiveness — and eventually, boos in the fifth round — in the humdrum title fight.
Barboza calls it a career after loss at UFC 330
Edson Barboza left his fight gloves on the mat and choked back tears as he retired following a lightweight loss on the main card to Esteben Ribovics.
The 40-year-old Barboza received a standing ovation and was flanked by his family as he officially called it quits after an MMA career that began in 2009. He made his UFC debut a year later and won multiple Fight of the Night honors. He lost the last four fights of his career.
“Every single fight, I promise I did my best,” Barboza said from inside the cage.
Barboza dropped to his knees and bowed his head as he lay down his gloves and was consoled by UFC ring announcer Bruce Buffer as he made the final walk back to the locker room.
Different kind of Broad Street Bullies usher in UFC’s return to Philadelphia
UFC held only its third numbered card in Philadelphia and first fight event overall in the city since 2019.
UFC 101 was held in August 2009, and UFC 133 was in August 2011.
Philly fight fans were in the mood to make up for lost time and about packed the arena and were wild for the punishing action the preliminary fights delivered hours before the main card was set to start.
It’s a perfect fit for a city that loves their bullies.
The fans got an early reward when 39-year-old Philly fighter Jeremiah Wells — who was booed on his walkout — won via submission on the card’s opening night and won over the inhospitable fans.
Tresean Gore won his middleweight fight, but lost his teeth in a unanimous decision victory over Vicente Luque.
Gore took a knee to his mouth and lost most of his bottom front teeth. They littered the cage and the fight official picked at least one up with his gloved hand. Gore pulled down his lower lip to show the bloody results as he talked to fight announcer Joe Rogan.
Charles Johnson celebrated his submission victory by leading the crowd in an off-key rendition of “Fly, Eagles, Fly.” It helps to pander. He walked out of the cage to a big ovation.

Taiwan household disposable income hits record NT$1.21 million
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-16
04:10:46 UTC
13:10:46 KST

TAIPEI (Taiwan News) — Taiwan's average household disposable income reached a record NT$1.21 million (US$38,500) in 2025, up 3.9% from a year earlier, according to a report issued Friday by the Directorate-General of Budget, Accounting and Statistics.
Disposable income refers to income remaining after non-consumption expenditures such as taxes and social insurance premiums have been deducted, leaving money available for consumption or savings, per Storm Media.
Hsinchu retained its position as the municipality with the highest average household disposable income at NT$1.604 million, followed by Hsinchu County at NT$1.569 million. Taipei ranked third at NT$1.554 million per household.
Hsinchu's high ranking was attributed to its concentration of high-tech companies in the Hsinchu Science Park and the growth of the AI industry. Taipei, meanwhile, benefits from its position as Taiwan's political and financial center, per CNA.
Among Taiwan's six major municipalities, Taipei, New Taipei, Taoyuan, and Taichung all recorded average household disposable income above the national average of NT$1.21 million. Tainan and Kaohsiung were below the national average, with household disposable income of NT$1.044 million and NT$1.206 million, respectively.
DGBAS added that average household consumption expenditure reached NT$920,000 in 2025, an increase of 3.6% from 2024. Average household savings rose 4.9% to NT$290,000 during the same period, per the report.

US Representative McCaul warns warns of China's belligerence toward Taiwan
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-16
04:10:20 UTC
13:10:20 KST

TAIPEI (Taiwan News) — US Rep. Michael McCaul, chair emeritus of the House Foreign Affairs Committee, warned that China's increasingly belligerent threats toward Taiwan pose a direct challenge to the global balance of power during his third visit to Taiwan, per VOA.
McCaul, a Republican from Texas, visited Taiwan from Aug. 2-7, meeting with President Lai Ching-te (賴清德), Vice President Hsiao Bi-khim (蕭美琴), and Foreign Minister Lin Chia-lung (林佳龍). He also delivered a speech at the annual Ketagalan Forum, where he reiterated US support under the Taiwan Relations Act.
"At a time when the stakes couldn't be higher, I was proud to visit Taiwan for the third time to reaffirm the United States' unwavering support," McCaul said in a statement. "The increasing belligerence of the Chinese Communist Party poses a direct threat — not only to Taiwan, but to the entire global balance of power," per a press release.
McCaul said he has consistently supported Taiwan, including efforts to advance the 2024 Supplemental Appropriations Act and strengthen US-Taiwan economic relations. He also highlighted his support for closer security cooperation among the US, Australia, and the United Kingdom. In recognition of his support for Taiwan, Lai awarded McCaul the Grand Cordon of the Order of the Brilliant Star.
McCaul previously announced that he would not seek reelection after his current term in Congress expires.
During his visit, McCaul also met with opposition leaders, including Legislative Yuan Speaker Han Kuo-yu (韓國瑜), and legislators from opposition parties. Discussions covered Taiwan's recently passed defense budget, the importance of drones, and US-Taiwan cooperation on drone production.
Before leaving Taiwan, McCaul also met with officials from the National Security Council and Ministry of National Defense to exchange views on strengthening Taiwan's defenses against China's coercive actions in the region. He also visited US drone company Shield AI and the Industrial Technology Research Institute, where he learned about Taiwan's drone industry and ITRI's certification work.
ITRI is the first institution outside the US authorized to certify that drones do not contain components from China, per VOA.
McCaul, a member of the House of Representatives Taiwan Caucus, first visited Taiwan in April 2023 as chair of the House Foreign Affairs Committee. He returned in May 2024 to attend Lai's inauguration.
China conducted military exercises involving aircraft and naval forces around Taiwan during both of those visits and imposed sanctions on McCaul. During his latest visit, McCaul said China's coercive actions had only strengthened his commitment to supporting a free and peaceful Taiwan.

Taiwan tracks 11 Chinese military aircraft and 10 ships
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-16
04:10:00 UTC
13:10:00 KST

TAIPEI (Taiwan News) — The Ministry of National Defense tracked 11 Chinese military aircraft, eight naval vessels, and two official ships between 6 a.m. on Saturday and the same time Sunday.
In response, Taiwan deployed aircraft, naval ships, and coastal-based missile systems. Seven of the People’s Liberation Army aircraft crossed the Taiwan Strait median line in the country’s northern and central air defense identification zones, or ADIZ, according to the ministry.
So far this month, Taiwan has tracked Chinese military aircraft 126 times and ships 189 times. Since September 2020, China has increased its use of gray zone tactics by incrementally increasing the number of military aircraft and naval vessels operating around Taiwan.
Gray zone tactics are defined as “an effort or series of efforts beyond steady-state deterrence and assurance that attempts to achieve one’s security objectives without resort to direct and sizable use of force.”

‘Proud to be a dimagi naxal’: P Chidambaram hits back at PM Modi

‘Proud to be a dimagi naxal’: P Chidambaram hits back at PM Modi
TOI News Desk / TIMESOFINDIA.COM / Updated: Aug 16, 2026, 12:36 IST
Comments
Share
AA
Text Size
Small
Medium
Large
File photo: PM Modi and senior Congress leader P Chidambaram
NEW DELHI: Former Union minister and senior Congress leader P Chidambaram on Sunday hit back at Prime Minister Narendra Modi over his “dimagi naxal” remarks, saying he was “proud” to be described by the term.“I am proud to be a dimagi naxal!” Chidambaram said in a post on X, a day after PM Modi, in his 80th Independence Day address from the Red Fort, warned that although armed Naxalism was nearing its end, people with an ideological Naxal mindset continued to pose a threat.
PM Modi had urged people to “identify and isolate” such individuals, saying they were looking for opportunities to promote violence and unrest and “drag the country on the wrong path”.
The Prime Minister said his government had made ending Naxalism a priority after coming to power in 2014. He said decades of Maoist violence had destroyed the lives and aspirations of young people and claimed that more than 3,500 security personnel had been killed in the conflict.“Naxalism, Maoism destroyed the dreams of lakhs of youth. It stole the sons of numerous mothers, crushed the dreams of numerous mothers,” PM Modi said in his Independence Day address.
He also alleged that people with a Maoist mindset had earlier occupied positions of influence in government committees and policymaking.
“For years, people with Maoist thinking were there in public life, even in government committees this thinking had affected various institutions and initiatives,” PM Modi said, before calling for the “dimagi naxal” to be identified and isolated.
Congress attacks PM Modi’s ‘dimagi naxal’ remark
Chidambaram's response came a day after Congress had already attacked PM Modi over the remarks.Congress general secretary Jairam Ramesh accused the Prime Minister of reviving the “urban naxal” label to target political opponents. He argued that the government had previously used the term despite Union home minister Amit Shah clarifying in Parliament that there was no official definition of “urban Naxal”.Ramesh also alleged that the government eventually adopted some of the issues raised by people it had labelled “urban Naxals”. He cited the caste census as an example, saying the idea had earlier been dismissed as reflecting “urban Naxal” thinking before the government announced a caste-based census.“First, you make derogatory remarks--calling them 'Urban Naxals' or 'Mental Naxals'--but later, you accept the very demands your political opponents were making,” Ramesh said, according to news agency ANI.The Congress leader had also earlier called PM Modi a “master abuser” in “Entire Political Science” while reacting to his use of the “urban naxal” and “dimagi naxal” labels.
The broader opposition has also criticised PM Modi's remarks. CPI(M) general secretary M A Baby said his party opposed Naxalism but accused the government of using the “Naxal mentality” label to target political opponents.CPI general secretary D Raja described “dimagi naxal” as an attempt to stigmatise dissent.TMC leader Saket Gokhale similarly accused PM Modi of using the Independence Day platform to take “cheap shots” at his critics.
PM Modi says armed Naxalism ‘breathing its last’
PM Modi's remarks came as he declared that the government had made substantial progress in tackling armed Naxalism.He said Naxalism had kept large parts of the country and its population “hostage” for decades and had resulted in the deaths of thousands of security personnel.
“In 2014, when you gave us the opportunity we had decided that we will rid the country of naxalism, and today I am happy to announce that naxalism does not have even the strength for breathing,” PM Modi said.At the same time, he cautioned that the end of armed insurgency did not mean the ideological challenge had disappeared.
“Even if these naxals are gone, but the 'dimagi naxal' (people with naxal thinking), are looking for an opportunity, looking to see ways of violence, and trying to drag the country to a wrong path,” PM Modi said.He linked the issue to his broader call for young people to contribute to the government's vision of a developed India by 2047, arguing that remote areas once affected by Naxal violence were now seeing development.
